summary: In Greek mythology, Leitus (Leïtos) is a Boeotian captain in the Trojan War — admiral of twelve ships in some tallies — who also sails with the Argonauts and ranks among Helen's suitors. Homer and later catalogues place him among the Boeotian leaders; Pausanias knows him as the only Boeotian chieftain to return safely from Troy, bringing home the bones of Arcesilaus.

sections.heading: Family and command
paragraphs: Homer's Catalogue sets Leitus among the Boeotian leaders from Hyria, Aulis, and the surrounding towns. Parentage varies: son of Alector (Alectryon) and Polybule, or of Lacritus and Cleobule; brother of Clonius; sometimes half-sibling to Arcesilaus and Prothoenor. A minority notice makes him earth-born, a son of Gaia.

Apollodorus counts him among the Argonauts and among Helen's suitors. At Troy he kills Phylacus among others; Poseidon rallies him with Teucer, Thoas, Meriones, Antilochus, Peneleos, and Deipyrus when the Trojans press the ships. Hector wounds him on the wrist, yet he survives the war.

sections.heading: Return
paragraphs: Pausanias reports that Leitus alone of the Boeotian leaders came home, and that he buried Arcesilaus near Lebadea; his own tomb was shown at Plataea. The atlas keeps him distinct from obscure catalogue namesakes.
